newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel inflation-linked bonds finish lower.
newsitem.headline: Israel inflation-linked bonds finish lower.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked bonds closed lower again on Monday as traders took profits on the strong price run-up of the last two months, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: -0.12 pct at 168.72
* CPI-linked government bonds: -0.13 pct at 169.37
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.05 pct at 167.96
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years):
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct at 159.55
Volume was strong at 184 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds, traders said.

"Inflation-linked bonds continue to fall because of profit taking. Yields fell from 5.3 percent in August to 4.5 percent and its only normal that investors want to take profits," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.

In addition, traders noted, the Bank of Israel said last week it would resume issuing linked bonds after a lapse of several months, putting pressure on long bonds carrying terms of seven years or more.
"The government plans to raise almost one billion shekels in November by issuing linked bonds, and this affects the CPI-linked long bonds," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.
In contrast, unlinked bonds were steady to higher in active trading.
"Investors prefer now unlinked bonds and Makams. The economy is slowing down, and inflation is expected to be relatively low while interest rates remain high," Weisberg said.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds remained stable in thin trading.
"Investors stillt will happen with the dollar. Today the shekel rose and the dollar-linked bonds closed slightly lower, but activity continues to be very low," the Hapoalim trader said.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2490 shekels against 3.2670 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.25 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
